Definition:Deduction Rule: Let \mathcal L be the language of propositional logic. The Deduction Rule is the rule of inference: :From U, \mathbf A \vdash \mathbf B, one may infer U \vdash \mathbf A \implies \mathbf B where: :\mathbf A, \mathbf B are WFFs of propositional logic :U is a set of WFFs For a given proof system, the Deduction Rule can be either a basic rule of inference, or a derived rule.

Deduction Theorem: Let \mathscr H be instance 1 of a Hilbert proof system. Then the deduction rule: ::\dfrac{U,\mathbf A \vdash \mathbf B}{U \vdash \mathbf A \implies \mathbf B} is a derived rule for \mathscr H.

Soundness Theorem for Hilbert Proof System: Let \mathscr H be instance 1 of a Hilbert proof system. Let \mathrm{BI} be the formal semantics of boolean interpretations. Then \mathscr H is a sound proof system for \mathrm{BI}: :Every \mathscr H-theorem is a tautology.
Equivalence of Definitions of Dominate (Set Theory): Let S, T be sets. {{TFAE|def = Dominate (Set Theory)|view = Dominate|context = Set Theory
Element of Toset has at most One Immediate Successor: Let \struct {S, \preceq} be a toset. Let a \in S. Then a has at most one immediate successor.
Element of Toset has at most One Immediate Predecessor: Let \struct {S, \preceq} be a toset. Let a \in S. Then a has at most one immediate predecessor.
Equivalence of Definitions of Complex Inverse Tangent Function: {{TFAE|def = Complex Inverse Tangent Let S be the subset of the complex plane: :S = \C \setminus \set {0 + i, 0 - i}
Equivalence of Definitions of Complex Inverse Cotangent Function: {{TFAE|def = Complex Inverse Cotangent Let S be the subset of the complex plane: :S = \C \setminus \left\{{0 + i, 0 - i}\right\}

Equivalence of Definitions of Complex Inverse Hyperbolic Tangent: {{TFAE|def = Complex Inverse Hyperbolic Tangent Let S be the subset of the complex plane: :S = \C \setminus \left\{{-1 + 0 i, 1 + 0 i}\right\}

Equivalence of Definitions of Complex Inverse Hyperbolic Cotangent: {{TFAE|def = Complex Inverse Hyperbolic Cotangent Let S be the subset of the complex plane: :S = \C \setminus \left\{{-1 + 0 i, 1 + 0 i}\right\}
Natural Numbers form Inductive Set: Let \N denote the natural numbers as subset of the real numbers \R. Then \N is an inductive set.

Square Root of Complex Number in Cartesian Form: Let z \in \C be a complex number. Let z = x + i y where x, y \in \R are real numbers. Let z not be wholly real, that is, such that y \ne 0. Then the square root of z is given by: :z^{1/2} = \pm \paren {a + i b} where: {{begin-eqn a \sqrt {\frac {x + \sqrt {x^2 + y^2} } 2} ; b \frac y {\cmod y} \sqrt {\frac {-x + \sqrt {x^2 + y^2} } 2} ; {{end-eqn

Zero is Identity in Naturally Ordered Semigroup: Let \struct {S, \circ, \preceq} be a naturally ordered semigroup. Let 0 be the zero of \struct {S, \circ, \preceq}. Then 0 is the identity for \circ. That is: :\forall n \in S: n \circ 0 = n = 0 \circ n

Reduction Formula for Integral of Power of Sine: Let n \in \Z_{> 0} be a (strictly) positive integer. Then: : \int \sin^n x \rd x = \dfrac {n - 1} n \int \sin^{n - 2} x \rd x - \dfrac {\sin^{n - 1} x \cos x} n is a reduction formula for \int \sin^n x \rd x.

Reduction Formula for Definite Integral of Power of Sine: Let n \in \Z_{> 0} be a positive integer. Let I_n be defined as: : I_n = \int_0^{\frac \pi 2} \sin^n x \rd x Then \left\langle{I_n}\right\rangle is a decreasing sequence of real numbers which satisfies: :n I_n = \left({n - 1}\right) I_{n - 2} Thus: :I_n = \dfrac {n - 1} n I_{n - 2} is a reduction formula for I_n.
Stirling's Formula/Proof 2/Lemma 4: Let I_n be defined as: : I_n = \int_0^{\frac \pi 2} \sin^n x \rd x Then: : \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \frac {I_{2 n} } {I_{2 n + 1} } = 1
Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Even Power of Sine x: \int_0^{\frac \pi 2} \sin^{2 n} x \rd x = \dfrac {\paren {2 n}!} {\paren {2^n n!}^2} \dfrac \pi 2
Definite Integral from 0 to Half Pi of Odd Power of Sine x: \int_0^{\frac \pi 2} \sin^{2 n + 1} x \rd x = \dfrac {\paren {2^n n!}^2} {\paren {2 n + 1}!}
Zero Complement is Not Empty: Let \struct {S, \circ, \preceq} be a naturally ordered semigroup. Let S^* be the zero complement of S. Then S^* is not empty.
Stirling's Formula/Proof 2/Lemma 5: \dfrac {n!} {n^n \sqrt n e^{-n} } \to \sqrt {2 \pi} as n \to \infty

Limit of Error in Stirling's Formula: Consider Stirling's Formula: :n! \sim \sqrt {2 \pi n} \left({\dfrac n e}\right)^n The ratio of n! to its approximation \sqrt {2 \pi n} \left({\dfrac n e}\right)^n is bounded as follows: :e^{1 / \left({12 n + 1}\right)} \le \dfrac {n!} {\sqrt {2 \pi n} n^n e^{-n} } \le e^{1 / 12 n}
Zero Strictly Precedes One: Let \left({S, \circ, \preceq}\right) be a naturally ordered semigroup. Let 0 be the zero of S. Let 1 be the one of S. Then: :0 \prec 1
Stirling's Formula/Proof 2/Lemma 2: The sequence \left \langle {d_n} \right \rangle defined as: : d_n = \ln \left({n!}\right) - \left({n + \frac 1 2}\right) \ln n + n is decreasing.
Ordering in terms of Addition: Let \left({S, \circ, \preceq}\right) be a naturally ordered semigroup. Then \forall m, n \in S: :m \preceq n \iff \exists p \in S: m \circ p = n

Difference in Naturally Ordered Semigroup is Unique: Let \struct {S, \circ, \preceq} be a naturally ordered semigroup. Let n, m \in S such that m \preceq n. Then there exists a unique difference n - m of m and n.
Equivalence of Definitions of Beta Function: {{TFAE|def = Beta Function For \map \Re x, \map \Re y > 0
Ordering of Naturally Ordered Semigroup is Strongly Compatible: \forall m, n, p \in S: m \preceq n \iff m \circ p \preceq n \circ p
Strict Ordering of Naturally Ordered Semigroup is Strongly Compatible: \forall m, n, p \in S: m \prec n \iff m \circ p \prec n \circ p

Sum with One is Immediate Successor in Naturally Ordered Semigroup: Let \left({S, \circ, \preceq}\right) be a naturally ordered semigroup. Let 1 be the one of S. Let n \in S. Then n \circ 1 is the immediate successor of n. That is, for all m \in S: :n \prec m \iff n \circ 1 \preceq m

Riemann Zeta Function at Even Integers: The Riemann \zeta function can be calculated for even integers as follows: {{begin-eqn \map \zeta {2 n} \paren {-1}^{n + 1} \dfrac {B_{2 n} 2^{2 n - 1} \pi^{2 n} } {\paren {2 n}!} ; r = \frac 1 {1^{2 n} } + \frac 1 {2^{2 n} } + \frac 1 {3^{2 n} } + \frac 1 {4^{2 n} } + \cdots ; {{end-eqn where: :B_n are the Bernoulli numbers :n is a positive integer.
Tangent Inequality: x < \tan x for all x in the interval \left({0 \,.\,.\, \dfrac {\pi} 2}\right).

Integral Representation of Riemann Zeta Function in terms of Gamma Function: For \Re \paren s > 1, the Riemann Zeta function is given by: : \map \zeta s = \frac 1 {\map \Gamma s} \int_0^\infty \frac {t^{s - 1 {e^t - 1} \rd t where \Gamma is the Gamma function.

Gamma Function is Unique Extension of Factorial: Let f: \R_{>0} \to \R be a real function which is positive and continuous. Let \ln \mathop \circ f be convex on \R_{>0}. Let f satisfy the conditions: :f \left({x + 1}\right) = \begin{cases} 1 & : x = 0 \\ x f \left({x}\right) & : x > 0 \end{cases} Then: : \forall x \in \R_{>0}: f \left({x}\right) = \Gamma \left({x}\right) where \Gamma \left({x}\right) is the Gamma function.
Equivalence of Definitions of Convex Real Function: Let f be a real function which is defined on a real interval I. {{TFAE|def = Convex Real Function
Equivalence of Definitions of Concave Real Function: Let f be a real function which is defined on a real interval I. {{TFAE|def = Concave Real Function

Power Series Expansion for Real Arcsine Function: The (real) arcsine function has a Taylor series expansion: {{begin-eqn \arcsin x \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\paren {2 n}!} {2^{2 n} \paren {n!}^2} \frac {x^{2 n + 1} } {2 n + 1} ; r = x + \frac 1 2 \frac {x^3} 3 + \frac {1 \times 3} {2 \times 4} \frac {x^5} 5 + \frac {1 \times 3 \times 5} {2 \times 4 \times 6} \frac {x^7} 7 + \cdots ; {{end-eqn which converges for -1 \le x \le 1.
Real Function is Concave iff its Negative is Convex: Let f be a real function. Let I \subseteq \R be an interval of \R. Then f is concave on I {{iff -f is convex on \R.
Equivalence of Definitions of Strictly Concave Real Function: Let f be a real function which is defined on a real interval I. {{TFAE|def = Strictly Concave Real Function
Equivalence of Definitions of Strictly Convex Real Function: Let f be a real function which is defined on a real interval I. {{TFAE|def = Strictly Convex Real Function

Concave Real Function is Left-Hand and Right-Hand Differentiable: Let f be a real function which is concave on the open interval \left({a \,.\,.\, b}\right). Then the left-hand derivative f'_- \left({x}\right) and right-hand derivative f'_+ \left({x}\right) both exist for all x \in \left({a \,.\,.\, b}\right).
Concave Real Function is Continuous: Let f be a real function which is concave on the open interval \left({a \,.\,.\, b}\right). Then f is continuous on \left({a \,.\,.\, b}\right).
Absolute Value Function is Convex: Let f: \R \to \R be the absolute value function on the real numbers. Then f is convex.

Real Function is Concave iff Derivative is Decreasing: Let f be a real function which is differentiable on the open interval \openint a b. Then f is concave on \openint a b {{iff its derivative f' is decreasing on \openint a b. Thus the intuitive result that a concave function "gets less steep".

Real Function is Strictly Convex iff Derivative is Strictly Increasing: Let f be a real function which is differentiable on the open interval \openint a b. Then f is strictly convex on \openint a b {{iff its derivative f' is strictly increasing on \openint a b.

Real Function is Strictly Concave iff Derivative is Strictly Decreasing: Let f be a real function which is differentiable on the open interval \openint a b. Then f is strictly concave on \openint a b {{iff its derivative f' is strictly decreasing on \openint a b.

Inverse of Strictly Decreasing Convex Real Function is Convex: Let f be a real function which is convex on the open interval I. Let J = f \left[{I}\right]. If f be strictly decreasing on I, then f^{-1} is convex on J.

Inverse of Strictly Increasing Concave Real Function is Convex: Let f be a real function which is concave on the open interval I. Let J = f \sqbrk I. If f is strictly increasing on I, then f^{-1} is convex on J.

Inverse of Strictly Decreasing Concave Real Function is Concave: Let f be a real function which is concave on the open interval I. Let J = f \left[{I}\right]. If f be strictly decreasing on I, then f^{-1} is concave on J.

Mean Value of Concave Real Function: Let f be a real function which is continuous on the closed interval \left[{a \,.\,.\, b}\right] and differentiable on the open interval \left({a \,.\,.\, b}\right). Let f be concave on \left({a \,.\,.\, b}\right). Then: : \forall \xi \in \left({a \,.\,.\, b}\right): f \left({x}\right) - f \left({\xi}\right) \le f^{\prime} \left({\xi}\right) \left({x - \xi}\right)
Differentiable Bounded Concave Real Function is Constant: Let f be a real function which is: :(1): \quad Differentiable on \R :(2): \quad Bounded on \R :(3): \quad Concave on \R. Then f is constant.

Second Derivative of Strictly Concave Real Function is Strictly Negative: Let f be a real function which is twice differentiable on the open interval \left({a \,.\,.\, b}\right). Then f is strictly concave on \left({a \,.\,.\, b}\right) {{iff its second derivative f < 0 on \left({a \,.\,.\, b}\right).

Second Derivative of Strictly Convex Real Function is Strictly Positive: Let f be a real function which is twice differentiable on the open interval \openint a b. Then f is strictly convex on \openint a b {{iff its second derivative f > 0 on \openint a b.

Inverse of Strictly Decreasing Strictly Convex Real Function is Strictly Convex: Let f be a real function which is strictly convex on the open interval I. Let J = f \sqbrk I. If f be strictly decreasing on I, then f^{-1} is strictly convex on J.

Inverse of Strictly Decreasing Strictly Concave Real Function is Strictly Concave: Let f be a real function which is strictly concave on the open interval I. Let J = f \left[{I}\right]. If f be strictly decreasing on I, then f^{-1} is strictly concave on J.

Inverse of Strictly Increasing Strictly Convex Real Function is Strictly Concave: Let f be a real function which is strictly convex on the open interval I. Let J = f \sqbrk I. If f be strictly increasing on I, then f^{-1} is strictly concave on J.

Inverse of Strictly Increasing Strictly Concave Real Function is Strictly Convex: Let f be a real function which is strictly concave on the open interval I. Let J = f \left[{I}\right]. If f be strictly increasing on I, then f^{-1} is strictly convex on J.

Gamma Function as Integral of Natural Logarithm: Let x \in \R_{>0} be a strictly positive real number. Then: : \map \Gamma x = \int_{\to 0}^1 \paren {\ln \frac 1 t}^{x - 1} \rd t where \Gamma denotes the Gamma function.
Reversal of Limits of Definite Integral: Let a \le b. Then: : \int_a^b \map f x \rd x = - \int_b^a \map f x \rd x

Beta Function is Defined for Positive Reals: Let x, y \in \R be real numbers. Let \Beta \left({x, y}\right) be the Beta function: : \Beta \left({x, y}\right) := \int_{\mathop \to 0}^{\mathop \to 1} t^{x - 1} \left({1 - t}\right)^{y - 1} \ \mathrm d t Then \Beta \left({x, y}\right) exists provided that x, y > 0.

Comparison Test for Improper Integral: Let I = \openint a b be an open real interval. Let \phi be a real function which is continuous on I and also non-negative on I. Let f be a real function which is continuous on I. Let f satisfy: :\forall x \in I: \size {\map f x} \le \map \phi x If the improper integral of \phi over I exists, then so does that of f.

Beta Function is Continuous and Positive on Positive Reals: Let x, y \in \R be real numbers. Let \map \Beta {x, y} be the Beta function: : \map \Beta {x, y} := \int_{\mathop \to 0}^{\mathop \to 1} t^{x - 1} \paren {1 - t}^{y - 1} \rd t Let y \in \R_{>0} be given. Then \map \Beta {x, y} is a positive and continuous function of x on \R_{>0}.

Logarithm of Beta Function is Convex on Positive Reals: Let x, y \in \R be real numbers. Let \Beta \left({x, y}\right) be the Beta function: : \Beta \left({x, y}\right) := \int_{\mathop \to 0}^{\mathop \to 1} t^{x - 1} \left({1 - t}\right)^{y - 1} \ \mathrm d t Let y \in \R_{>0} be given. Then \ln \left({\Beta \left({x, y}\right)}\right) is a convex function of x on \R_{>0}.

Gamma Function of One Half: \map \Gamma {\dfrac 1 2} = \sqrt \pi Its decimal expansion starts: :\map \Gamma {\dfrac 1 2} = 1 \cdotp 77245 \, 38509 \, 05516 \, 02729 \, 81674 \, 83341 \, 14518 \, 27975 \ldots
Integral of Exponent of Half Square over Reals: \int_{\mathop \to -\infty}^{\mathop \to +\infty} e^{- x^2 / 2} \rd x = \sqrt {2 \pi}
Sum of Reciprocals of Primes is Divergent/Proof 2: The series: : \sum_{p \mathop \in \Bbb P} \frac 1 p where: :\Bbb P is the set of all prime numbers is divergent.
Sum of Reciprocals of Primes is Divergent/Lemma: Let C \in \R_{>0} be a (strictly) positive real number. Then: : \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \paren {\map \ln {\ln n} - C} = + \infty

Strictly Increasing Infinite Sequence of Integers is Cofinal in Natural Numbers: Let S = \left\langle{x_n}\right\rangle be an infinite sequence of integers which is strictly increasing. Then S is a cofinal subset of \left({\Z, \le}\right) where \le is the usual ordering on the integers.

Product of Even and Odd Functions: Let \mathcal O be an odd real function defined on some symmetric set S. Let \mathcal E be an even real function defined on some symmetric set S'. Let \mathcal O\mathcal E be their pointwise product, defined on the intersection of the domains of \mathcal O and \mathcal E. Then \mathcal O\mathcal E is odd. That is: :\forall x \in S \cap S': \left({\mathcal O\mathcal E}\right)\left({-x}\right) = - \left({\mathcal O\mathcal E}\right)\left({x}\right).
Millin Series: The Millin series is the series defined as: : \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac 1 {F_{2^n = \frac {7 - \sqrt 5} 2
Odd Bernoulli Numbers Vanish: Let B_n denote the nth Bernoulli Number. Then: :B_{2n + 1} = 0 for n \ge 1.

Gauss Multiplication Formula: Let \Gamma denote the Gamma Function. Then: : \forall z \notin \set {-\frac m n: m \in \N}: \prod_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \map \Gamma {z + \frac k n} = \paren {2 \pi}^{\paren {n - 1} / 2} n^{1/2 - n z} \map \Gamma {n z} where \N denotes the natural numbers.
Dirichlet Integral: \int_0^\infty \frac {\sin x} x \rd x = \frac \pi 2

Riemann Zeta Function and Prime Counting Function: For \map \Re s > 1: : \log \map \zeta s = s \int_0^{\mathop \to \infty} \frac {\map \pi x} {x \paren {x^s - 1} } \rd x where: :\zeta denotes the Riemann Zeta Function :\pi denotes the Prime-Counting Function.

Faulhaber's Formula: Let n and p be positive integers. Then: : \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n k^p = \frac 1 {p + 1} \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^p \paren {-1}^i \binom {p + 1} i B_i n^{p + 1 - i} where B_n denotes the nth Bernoulli number.
Complex Exponential Tends to Zero: Let \exp z be the complex exponential function. Then: : \lim_{\map \Re z \mathop \to +\infty} e^{-z} = 0 where \map \Re z denotes the real part of z.

Modulus of Exponential is Exponential of Real Part: Let z \in \C be a complex number. Let \exp z denote the complex exponential function. Let \cmod {\, \cdot \,} denote the complex modulus Then: :\cmod {\exp z} = \map \exp {\Re z} where \Re z denotes the real part of z.

Laplace Transform of Exponential/Real Argument: Let \laptrans f denote the Laplace transform of a function f. Let e^x be the real exponential. Then: :\map {\laptrans {e^{a t} } } s = \dfrac 1 {s - a} where a \in \R is constant, and \map \Re s > \map \Re a.

Laplace Transform of Cosine: Let \cos be the real cosine function. Let \laptrans f denote the Laplace transform of the real function f. Then: :\laptrans {\cos a t} = \dfrac s {s^2 + a^2} where a \in \R_{>0} is constant, and \map \Re s > a.

Laplace Transform of Sine: Let \sin denote the real sine function. Let \laptrans f denote the Laplace transform of a real function f. Then: :\laptrans {\sin at} = \dfrac a {s^2 + a^2} where a \in \R_{>0} is constant, and \map \Re s > 0.

Sum Rule for Derivatives/General Result: Let f_1 \left({x}\right), f_2 \left({x}\right), \ldots, f_n \left({x}\right) be real functions all differentiable. Then for all n \in \N_{>0}: : D_x \left({\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n f_i \left({x}\right)}\right) = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n D_x \left({f_i \left({x}\right)}\right)

Product Rule for Derivatives/General Result: Let f_1 \left({x}\right), f_2 \left({x}\right), \ldots, f_n \left({x}\right) be real functions differentiable on the open interval I. then: :\forall x \in I: D_x \left({\prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n f_i \left({x}\right)}\right) = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \left({D_x \left({f_i \left({x}\right)}\right) \prod_{j \mathop \ne i} f_j \left({x}\right)}\right)
Derivative of Arccotangent Function: \dfrac {\map \d {\arccot x} } {\d x} = \dfrac {-1} {1 + x^2}
Derivative of Arcsecant Function/Corollary 2: \dfrac {\mathrm d \left({\operatorname{arcsec} x }\right)} {\mathrm d x} = \dfrac 1 {x^2 \sqrt {1 - \frac 1 {x^2}

Asymptotic Formula for Bernoulli Numbers: The Bernoulli numbers with even index can be approximated by the asymptotic formula: :B_{2 n} \sim \paren {-1}^{n + 1} 4 \sqrt {\pi n} \paren {\dfrac n {\pi e} }^{2 n} where: :B_n denotes the nth Bernoulli number :\sim denotes asymptotically equal.
Cotangent Minus Tangent: \cot x - \tan x = 2 \cot 2 x
Derivative of Hyperbolic Cotangent Function: \map {\dfrac \d {\d x} } {\coth u} = -\csch^2 u \dfrac {\d u} {\d x}
Derivative of Hyperbolic Cosecant Function: \map {\dfrac \d {\d x} } {\csch u} = -\csch u \coth u \dfrac {\d u} {\d x}
Derivative of Inverse Hyperbolic Sine: \map {\dfrac \d {\d x} } {\sinh^{-1} x} = \dfrac 1 {\sqrt {x^2 + 1} }
Derivative of Inverse Hyperbolic Cosine: \map {\dfrac \d {\d x} } {\cosh^{-1} x} = \dfrac 1 {\sqrt {x^2 - 1} }
Derivative of Inverse Hyperbolic Tangent: \map {\dfrac \d {\d x} } {\tanh^{-1} x} = \dfrac 1 {1 - x^2}
Derivative of Inverse Hyperbolic Cotangent: \map {\dfrac \d {\d x} } {\coth^{-1} x} = \dfrac {-1} {x^2 - 1}
Derivative of Inverse Hyperbolic Secant: \map {\dfrac \d {\d x} } {\sech^{-1} x} = \dfrac {-1} {x \sqrt{1 - x^2} }
Derivative of Inverse Hyperbolic Cosecant: \map {\dfrac \d {\d x} } {\csch^{-1} x} = \dfrac {-1} {\size x \sqrt {1 + x^2} }
Sum of Cosecant and Cotangent: \csc x + \cot x = \cot {\frac x 2}

Leibniz's Rule/One Variable/Second Derivative: Let f and g be real functions defined on the open interval I. Let x \in I be a point in I at which both f and g are twice differentiable. Then: :\paren {\map f x \, \map g x} = \map f x \, \map {g} x + 2 \map {f'} x \, \map {g'} x + \map {f} x \, \map g x

Leibniz's Rule/One Variable/Third Derivative: Let f and g be real functions defined on the open interval I. Let x \in I be a point in I at which both f and g are thrice differentiable. Then: :\paren {\map f x \, \map g x} = \map f x \, \map {g} x + 3 \map {f'} x \, \map {g} x + 3 \map {f} x \, \map {g'} x + \map {f} x \, \map g x

Power Series Expansion for Tangent Function: The tangent function has a Taylor series expansion: {{begin-eqn \tan x \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^{n - 1} 2^{2 n} \paren {2^{2 n} - 1} B_{2 n} \, x^{2 n - 1} } {\paren {2 n}!} ; r = x + \frac {x^3} 3 + \frac {2 x^5} {15} + \frac {17 x^7} {315} + \cdots ; {{end-eqn where B_{2 n} denotes the Bernoulli numbers. This converges for \size x < \dfrac \pi 2.

Partial Differentiation Operator is Commutative for Continuous Functions: Let \map f {x, y} be a function of the two independent variables x and y. Let \map f {x, y} be continuous. Let the partial deriviatives of f also be continuous. Then: :\dfrac {\partial^2 f} {\partial x \partial y} = \dfrac {\partial^2 f} {\partial y \partial x}
Primitive of Constant Multiple of Function: Let f be a real function which is integrable. Let c be a constant. Then: : \int c \map f x \rd x = c \int \map f x \rd x

Primitive of Pointwise Sum of Functions: Let f_1, f_2, \ldots, f_n be real functions which are integrable. Then: : \int \map {\paren {f_1 \pm f_2 \pm \, \cdots \pm f_n} } x \rd x = \int \map {f_1} x \rd x \pm \int \map {f_2} x \rd x \pm \, \cdots \pm \int \map {f_n} x \rd x

Hurwitz's Theorem (Number Theory): Let \xi be an irrational number. Then there are infinitely many relatively prime integers m, n \in \Z such that: :\left|{\xi - \dfrac p q}\right| < \dfrac 1 {\sqrt 5 \, q^2}
Primitive of Function of Constant Multiple: Let f be a real function which is integrable. Let c be a constant. Then: : \int \map f {c x} \rd x = \frac 1 c \int \map f u \d u where u = c x.

Primitive of Composite Function: Let f and g be a real functions which are integrable. Let the composite function g \circ f also be integrable. Then: {{begin-eqn \int \map {\paren {g \circ f} } x \rd x \int \map g u \frac {\d x} {\d u} \rd u ; r = \int \frac {\map g u} {\map {f'} x} \rd u ; {{end-eqn where u = \map f x.

Weierstrass Product Inequality: For n \ge 1: : \prod_{i \mathop = 1}^n \left({1 - a_i}\right) \ge 1 - \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n a_i where all of a_i are in the closed interval \left[{0 \,.\,.\,1 }\right].
Primitive of Power: Let n \in \R: n \ne -1. Then: : \int x^n \rd x = \frac {x^{n + 1} } {n + 1} + C where C is an arbitrary constant. That is: :\dfrac {x^{n + 1} } {n + 1} is a primitive of x^n.
Sine Inequality: \size {\sin x} \le \size x for all x \in \R.
Jordan's Inequality: \dfrac 2 {\pi} x \le \sin x \le x for all x in the interval \left[{0 \,.\,.\, \dfrac {\pi} 2}\right]
Cosine Inequality: 1 - \dfrac {x^2} 2 \le \cos x for all x \in \R.

Laplace Transform of Constant Mapping: Let a \in \R be a real constant. Let f_a: \R \to \R or \C be the constant mapping, defined as: :\forall t \in \R: \map {f_a} t = a Let \laptrans {f_a} be the Laplace transform of f_a. Then: :\laptrans {\map {f_a} t} = \dfrac a s for \map \Re s > a.

Laplace Transform of Identity Mapping: Let \laptrans f denote the Laplace transform of a function f. Let \map {I_\R} t denote the identity mapping on \R for t > 0. Then: :\laptrans {\map {I_\R} t} = \dfrac 1 {s^2} for \map \Re s > 0.

Laplace Transform of Positive Integer Power: Let \laptrans f denote the Laplace transform of a function f. Let t^n: \R \to \R be t to the nth power for some n \in \N_{\ge 0}. Then: :\laptrans {t^n} = \dfrac {n!} { s^{n + 1} } for \map \Re s > 0.

Primitive of Function under its Derivative: Let f be a real function which is integrable. Then: : \int \frac {\map {f'} x} {\map f x} \rd x = \ln \size {\map f x} + C where C is an arbitrary constant.
Primitive of Exponential Function/General Result: Let a \in \R_{>0} be a constant such that a \ne 1. Then: : \int a^x \rd x = \frac {a^x} {\ln a} + C where C is an arbitrary constant.
Primitive of Tangent Function/Secant Form: \int \tan x \rd x = \ln \size {\sec x} + C where \sec x is defined.
Primitive of Secant Function/Tangent plus Angle Form: \int \sec x \rd x = \ln \size {\map \tan {\frac x 2 + \frac \pi 4} } + C
Exponential of x not less than 1+x: e^x \ge 1 + x for all x \in \R.
Primitive of Cosecant Function/Cosecant minus Cotangent Form: \int \csc x \rd x = \ln \size {\csc x - \cot x} + C where \csc x - \cot x \ne 0.
Primitive of Cosecant Function/Tangent Form: \int \csc x \rd x = \ln \size {\tan \frac x 2} + C where \tan \dfrac x 2 \ne 0.
Primitive of Square of Secant Function: \int \sec^2 x \rd x = \tan x + C where C is an arbitrary constant.
Primitive of Square of Cosecant Function: \int \csc^2 x \rd x = -\cot x + C where C is an arbitrary constant.
Primitive of Square of Tangent Function: \int \tan^2 x \rd x = \tan x - x + C
Primitive of Square of Cotangent Function: \int \cot^2 x \rd x = -\cot x - x + C where C is an arbitrary constant.
Primitive of Square of Sine Function: \int \sin^2 x \rd x = \frac x 2 - \frac {\sin 2 x} 4 + C where C is an arbitrary constant.
Primitive of Square of Cosine Function: \int \cos^2 x \rd x = \frac x 2 + \frac {\sin 2 x} 4 + C
Primitive of Product of Secant and Tangent: \int \sec x \tan x \rd x = \sec x + C where C is an arbitrary constant.
Primitive of Product of Cosecant and Cotangent: \int \csc x \cot x \rd x = -\csc x + C where C is an arbitrary constant.
Primitive of Hyperbolic Sine Function: \int \sinh x \rd x = \cosh x + C
Primitive of Hyperbolic Cosine Function: \int \cosh x \rd x = \sinh x + C
Primitive of Hyperbolic Tangent Function: \int \tanh x \rd x = \map \ln {\cosh x} + C
Primitive of Hyperbolic Cotangent Function: \int \coth x \rd x = \ln \size {\sinh x} + C where \sinh x \ne 0.
Limit of Tan X over X: \lim_{x \mathop \to 0} \frac {\tan x} x = 1
Euler Formula for Sine Function/Real Numbers: \sin x = x \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {1 - \frac {x^2} {n^2 \pi^2} } for all x \in \R.
Euler Formula for Sine Function/Complex Numbers: \sin z = z \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \left({1 - \frac {z^2} {n^2 \pi^2\right) for all z \in \C.
Logarithm of Reciprocal: \map {\log_b} {\dfrac 1 x} = -\log_b x
Primitive of Hyperbolic Secant Function/Arcsine Form: \int \sech x \rd x = \map \arcsin {\tanh x} + C
Primitive of Hyperbolic Secant Function/Arctangent of Exponential Form: \int \sech x \rd x = 2 \map \arctan {e^x} + C
Primitive of Hyperbolic Cosecant Function/Logarithm Form: \int \csch x \rd x = -\ln \size {\csch x + \coth x} + C where \csch x + \coth x \ne 0.
Primitive of Hyperbolic Cosecant Function/Hyperbolic Tangent Form: \int \csch x \rd x = \ln \size {\tanh \frac x 2} + C where \tanh \dfrac x 2 \ne 0.
Primitive of Hyperbolic Cosecant Function/Inverse Hyperbolic Cotangent Form: \int \csch x \rd x = -2 \map {\coth^{-1} } {e^x} + C
Primitive of Square of Hyperbolic Secant Function: \int \sech^2 x \rd x = \tanh x + C where C is an arbitrary constant.
Primitive of Square of Hyperbolic Cosecant Function: \int \csch^2 x \rd x = -\coth x + C where C is an arbitrary constant.
Primitive of Square of Hyperbolic Tangent Function: \int \tanh^2 x \rd x = x - \tanh x + C where C is an arbitrary constant.
Primitive of Square of Hyperbolic Cotangent Function: \int \coth^2 x \rd x = x - \coth x + C where C is an arbitrary constant.

Heaviside Step Function is Piecewise Continuous: Let c \ge 0 be a constant real number. The Heaviside step function: :\mu_c \left({t}\right) = \begin{cases} 1 & : t > c \\ 0 & : t < c \end{cases} is piecewise continuous for any interval of the form: :\left[{c - M \,.\,.\, c + M}\right] where M > 0 is some arbitrarily large constant.
Euler Formula for Sine Function/Complex Numbers/Proof 1/Lemma 1: The function: :\dfrac {\sinh x} x is increasing for positive real x.
Hyperbolic Tangent Less than X: \tanh x \le x for x \ge 0.
Primitive of Square of Hyperbolic Sine Function: \int \sinh^2 x \rd x = \frac {\sinh 2 x} 4 - \frac x 2 + C where C is an arbitrary constant.
Primitive of Square of Hyperbolic Cosine Function: \int \cosh^2 x \rd x = \frac {\sinh 2 x} 4 + \frac x 2 + C where C is an arbitrary constant.
Primitive of Product of Hyperbolic Secant and Tangent: \int \sech x \tanh x \rd x = -\sech x + C where C is an arbitrary constant.
Primitive of Product of Hyperbolic Cosecant and Cotangent: \int \csch x \coth x \rd x = -\csch x + C where C is an arbitrary constant.

Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared minus a squared/Logarithm Form 2: \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 - a^2} = \frac 1 {2 a} \ln \size {\frac {x - a} {x + a} } + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of a squared minus x squared/Logarithm Form 1: \int \frac {\d x} {a^2 - x^2} = \begin {cases} \dfrac 1 {2 a} \map \ln {\dfrac {a + x} {a - x} } + C & : \size x < a\\ & \\ \dfrac 1 {2 a} \map \ln {\dfrac {x + a} {x - a} } + C & : \size x > a \\ & \\ \text {undefined} & : \size x = a \end {cases}

Primitive of Reciprocal of a squared minus x squared: thumb|right|600px|\color {blue} {\dfrac 1 {a^2 - x^2} } \qquad \color {red} {\dfrac 1 a \tanh^{-1} \dfrac x a} \qquad \color {green} {\dfrac 1 a \coth^{-1} \dfrac x a} Let a \in \R_{>0} be a strictly positive real constant.
Primitive of Reciprocal of Root of x squared plus a squared/Logarithm Form: \int \frac {\d x} {\sqrt {x^2 + a^2} } = \map \ln {x + \sqrt {x^2 + a^2} } + C

Limit at Infinity of Polynomial over Complex Exponential: Let n \in \N. Let \map {P_n} x be a real polynomial, of degree n. Let e^z be the complex exponential function, where z = x + i y. Let a \in \R_{>0}. Then: : \lim_{x \mathop \to +\infty} \frac {\map {P_n} x} {e^{a z} } = 0

Primitive of Reciprocal of Root of x squared minus a squared/Logarithm Form: \int \frac {\d x} {\sqrt {x^2 - a^2} } = \ln \size {x + \sqrt {x^2 - a^2} } + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of x by Root of x squared minus a squared: \int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt {x^2 - a^2} } = \frac 1 a \arcsec \size {\frac x a} + C for \size x > a.
Primitive of Reciprocal of x by Root of x squared plus a squared/Logarithm Form: \int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt {x^2 + a^2} } = -\frac 1 a \map \ln {\frac {a + \sqrt {x^2 + a^2} } x} + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of x by Root of a squared minus x squared/Logarithm Form: \int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt {a^2 - x^2} } = -\frac 1 a \map \ln {\frac {a + \sqrt {a^2 - x^2} } x} + C
Primitive of Function of a x + b: \int \map F {a x + b} \rd x = \frac 1 a \int \map F u \rd u where u = a x + b.
Primitive of Function of Root of a x + b: \int F \left({\sqrt {a x + b\right) \ \mathrm d x = \frac 2 a \int u \ F \left({u}\right) \ \mathrm d u where u = \sqrt {a x + b}.

Derivative of Nth Root: Let n \in \N_{>0}. Let f: \R \to \R be the real function defined as f \left({x}\right) = \sqrt [n] x. Then: :f' \left({x}\right) = \dfrac 1 {n \left({\sqrt [n] x}\right)^{n-1} } everywhere that f \left({x}\right) = \sqrt [n] x is defined.
Primitive of Function of Nth Root of a x + b: \int F \left({\sqrt [n] {a x + b\right) \ \mathrm d x = \frac n a \int u^{n-1} F \left({u}\right) \ \mathrm d u where u = \sqrt [n] {a x + b}.
Primitive of Function of Root of a squared minus x squared: \int F \left({\sqrt {a^2 - x^2\right) \ \mathrm d x = a \int \cos u \ F \left({a \cos u}\right) \ \mathrm d u where x = a \sin u.
Primitive of Function of Root of a squared plus x squared: \int F \left({\sqrt {a^2 + x^2\right) \ \mathrm d x = a \int \sec^2 u \ F \left({a \sec u}\right) \ \mathrm d u where x = a \tan u.
Primitive of Function of Root of x squared minus a squared: \int F \left({\sqrt {x^2 - a^2\right) \ \mathrm d x = a \int \sec u \tan u \ F \left({a \tan u}\right) \ \mathrm d u where x = a \sec u.
Primitive of Function of Exponential Function: \int \map F {e^{a x} } \rd x = \frac 1 a \int \frac {\map F u} u \rd u where u = e^{a x}.
Primitive of Function of Natural Logarithm: \int F \left({\ln x}\right) \rd x = \int F \left({u}\right) e^u \rd u where u = \ln x.
Primitive of Function of Arcsine: \int F \left({\arcsin \frac x a}\right) \ \mathrm d x = a \int F \left({u}\right) \cos u \ \mathrm d u where u = \arcsin \dfrac x a.
Primitive of Function of Arccosine: \int F \paren {\arccos \frac x a} \rd x = -a \int F \paren u \sin u \rd u where u = \arccos \dfrac x a.
Primitive of Function of Arctangent: \int F \left({\arctan \frac x a}\right) \ \mathrm d x = a \int F \left({u}\right) \sec^2 u \ \mathrm d u where u = \arctan \dfrac x a.

Primitive of Function of Arccotangent: \int F \left({\operatorname{arccot} \frac x a}\right) \ \mathrm d x = -a \int F \left({u}\right) \csc^2 u \ \mathrm d u where u = \operatorname{arccot} \dfrac x a.
Primitive of Function of Arcsecant: \int \map F {\arcsec \frac x a} \rd x = a \int \map F u \sec u \tan u \rd u where u = \arcsec \dfrac x a.

Primitive of Function of Arccosecant: \int F \left({\operatorname{arccsc} \frac x a}\right) \ \mathrm d x = -a \int F \left({u}\right) \left\vert{\csc u}\right\vert \cot u \ \mathrm d u where u = \operatorname{arccsc} \dfrac x a.
Primitive of Reciprocal of a x + b: \int \frac {\d x} {a x + b} = \frac 1 a \ln \size {a x + b} + C
Primitive of x over a x + b: \int \frac {x \rd x} {a x + b} = \frac x a - \frac b {a^2} \ln \size {a x + b} + C
Laplace Transform of Exponential times Function: \laptrans {e^{a t} \map f t} = \map F {s - a} everywhere that \laptrans f exists, for \map \Re s > a

Laplace Transform of Derivative: Let f' be piecewise continuous with one-sided limits on said intervals. Then \laptrans f exists for \map \Re s > a, and: :\laptrans {\map {f'} t} = s \laptrans {\map f t} - \map f 0
Primitive of x squared over a x + b: \int \frac {x^2 \rd x} {a x + b} = \frac {\paren {a x + b}^2} {2 a^3} - \frac {2 b \paren {a x + b} } {a^3} + \frac {b^2} {a^3} \ln \size {a x + b} + C

Primitive of x cubed over a x + b: \int \frac {x^3 \rd x} {a x + b} = \frac {\paren {a x + b}^3} {3 a^4} - \frac {3 b \paren {a x + b}^2} {2 a^4} - \frac {3 b^2 \paren {a x + b} } {a^4} + \frac {b^3} {a^4} \ln \size {a x + b} + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of x by a x + b: \int \frac {\rd x} {x \paren {a x + b} } = \frac 1 b \ln \size {\frac x {a x + b} } + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by a x + b: \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 \paren {a x + b} } = -\frac 1 {b x} + \frac a {b^2} \ln \size {\frac {a x + b} x} + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of x cubed by a x + b: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} = \frac {2 a x - b} {2 b^2 x^2} + \frac {a^2} {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of a x + b squared: \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a x + b}^2} = -\frac 1 {a \paren {a x + b} } + C
Primitive of x over a x + b squared: \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} = \frac b {a^2 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac 1 {a^2} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert + C
Primitive of x squared over a x + b squared: \int \frac {x^2 \rd x} {\paren {a x + b}^2} = \frac {a x + b} {a^3} - \frac {b^2} {a^3 \paren {a x + b} } - \frac {2 b} {a^3} \ln \size {a x + b} + C

Primitive of x cubed over a x + b squared: \int \frac {x^3 \ \mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} = \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} {2 a^4} - \frac {3 b \left({a x + b}\right)} {a^4} + \frac {b^3} {a^4 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {3 b^2} {a^4} \ln \left\vert{a x + b}\right\vert + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of x by a x + b squared: \int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {a x + b}^2} = \frac 1 {b \paren {a x + b} } + \frac 1 {b^2} \ln \size {\frac x {a x + b} } + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by a x + b squared: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} = \frac {-a} {b^2 \left({a x + b}\right)} - \frac 1 {b^2 x} + \frac {2 a} {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac {a x + b} x}\right\vert + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of x cubed by a x + b squared: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} = - \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^2} {2 b^4 x^2} + \frac {3 a \left({a x + b}\right)} {b^4 x} - \frac {a^3 x} {b^4 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac {3 a^2} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{\frac x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C
Primitives of Rational Functions involving a x + b squared: This page gathers together the primitives of some rational functions involving \left({a x + b}\right)^2.
Primitive of Reciprocal of a x + b cubed: \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a x + b}^3} = -\frac 1 {2 a \paren {a x + b}^2} + C
Primitive of x over a x + b cubed: \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^3} = \frac {-1} {a^2 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac b {2 a^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C

Primitive of x squared over a x + b cubed: \int \frac {x^2 \rd x} {\paren {a x + b}^3} = \frac {2 b} {a^3 \paren {a x + b} } - \frac {b^2} {2 a^3 \paren {a x + b}^2} + \frac 1 {a^3} \ln \size {a x + b} + C

Primitive of x cubed over a x + b cubed: \int \frac {x^3 \rd x} {\paren {a x + b}^3} = \frac x {a^3} - \frac {3 b^2} {a^4 \paren {a x + b} } + \frac {b^3} {2 a^4 \paren {a x + b}^2} - \frac {3 b} {a^4} \ln \size {a x + b} + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of x by a x + b cubed: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({a x + b}\right)^3} = \frac {a^2 x^2} {2 b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} - \frac {2 a x} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac 1 {b^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac x {a x + b} }\right\vert + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by a x + b cubed: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^3} = \frac {-a} {2 b^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} - \frac {2 a} {b^3 \left({a x + b}\right)} - \frac 1 {b^3 x} + \frac {3 a} {b^4} \ln \left\vert{\frac {a x + b} x}\right\vert + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of x cubed by a x + b cubed: \int \frac {\d x} {x^3 \paren {a x + b}^3} = \frac {a^4 x^2} {2 b^5 \paren {a x + b}^2} - \frac {4 a^3 x} {b^5 \paren {a x + b} } - \frac {\paren {a x + b}^2} {2 b^5 x^2} + \frac {4 a} {b^4 x} + \frac {6 a^2} {b^5} \ln \size {\frac x {a x + b} } + C

Laplace Transform of Hyperbolic Cosine: Let \cosh t be the hyperbolic cosine, where t is real. Let \laptrans f denote the Laplace transform of the real function f. Then: :\laptrans {\cosh a t} = \dfrac s {s^2 - a^2} where a \in \R_{>0} is constant, and \map \Re s > a.

Laplace Transform of Hyperbolic Sine: Let \sinh t be the hyperbolic sine, where t is real. Let \laptrans f denote the Laplace transform of the real function f. Then: :\laptrans {\sinh a t} = \dfrac a {s^2 - a^2} where a \in \R_{>0} is constant, and \map \Re s > a.
Primitives of Rational Functions involving a x + b cubed: This page gathers together the primitives of some rational functions involving \left({a x + b}\right)^3.
Primitive of Power of a x + b: \int \paren {a x + b}^n \rd x = \frac {\paren {a x + b}^{n + 1} } {\paren {n + 1} a} + C

Primitive of x by Power of a x + b: \int x \left({a x + b}\right)^n \ \mathrm d x = \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 2} } {\left({n + 2}\right) a^2} - \frac {b \left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 1} } {\left({n + 1}\right) a^2} + C

Primitive of x squared by Power of a x + b: \int x^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^n \ \mathrm d x = \frac {\left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 3} } {\left({n + 3}\right) a^3} - \frac {2 b \left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 2} } {\left({n + 2}\right) a^3} + \frac {b^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 1} } {\left({n + 1}\right) a^3} + C

Reduction Formula for Primitive of Power of x by Power of a x + b/Decrement of Power of a x + b: \int x^m \left({a x + b}\right)^n \rd x = \frac {x^{m+1} \left({a x + b}\right)^n} {m + n + 1} + \frac {n b} {m + n + 1} \int x^m \left({a x + b}\right)^{n - 1} \rd x
Primitive of x over a x + b cubed/Proof 1: \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^3} = \frac {-1} {a^2 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac b {2 a^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C
Primitive of x over a x + b cubed/Proof 2: \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {\left({a x + b}\right)^3} = \frac {-1} {a^2 \left({a x + b}\right)} + \frac b {2 a^2 \left({a x + b}\right)^2} + C

Distance from Subset to Element: Let \struct {M, d} be a metric space. Let S \subseteq M be a subset of M. Let s \in S. Then: :\map d {s, S} = 0 where \map d {s, S} denotes the distance between s and S.

Reduction Formula for Primitive of Power of x by Power of a x + b/Decrement of Power of x: \int x^m \left({a x + b}\right)^n \rd x = \frac {x^m \left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 1} } {\left({m + n + 1}\right) a} - \frac {m b} {\left({m + n + 1}\right) a} \int x^{m - 1} \left({a x + b}\right)^n \rd x

Distance from Subset to Supremum: Let S \subseteq \R be a subset of the real numbers. Suppose that the supremum \sup S of S exists. Then: :\map d {\sup S, S} = 0 where \map d {\sup S, S} is the distance between \sup S and S.

Distance between Element and Subset is Nonnegative: Let \struct {M, d} be a metric space. Let x \in M and S \subseteq M. Then: :\map d {x, S} \ge 0 where \map d {x, S} is the distance between x and S.

Distance from Subset to Infimum: Let S \subseteq \R be a subset of the real numbers. Suppose that the infimum \inf S of S exists. Then: :\map d {\inf S, S} = 0 where \map d {\inf S, S} is the distance between \inf S and S.

Reduction Formula for Primitive of Power of x by Power of a x + b/Increment of Power of a x + b: \int x^m \paren {a x + b}^n \rd x = \frac {-x^{m + 1} \paren {a x + b}^{n + 1} } {\paren {n + 1} b} + \frac {m + n + 2} {\paren {n + 1} b} \int x^m \paren {a x + b}^{n + 1} \rd x

Reduction Formula for Primitive of Power of x by Power of a x + b/Increment of Power of x: \int x^m \left({a x + b}\right)^n \rd x = \frac {x^{m+1} \left({a x + b}\right)^{n + 1} } {\left({m + 1}\right) b} - \frac {\left({m + n + 2}\right) a} {\left({m + 1}\right) b} \int x^{m + 1} \left({a x + b}\right)^n \rd x
Primitive of Reciprocal of Root of a x + b: \int \frac {\d x} {\sqrt{a x + b} } = \frac {2 \sqrt {a x + b} } a + C
Primitive of x over Root of a x + b: \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {\sqrt{a x + b} } = \frac {2 \left({a x - 2 b}\right) \sqrt{a x + b} } {3 a^2}

Signum Function is Completely Multiplicative: The signum function on the set of real numbers is a completely multiplicative function: :\forall x, y \in \R: \map \sgn {x y} = \map \sgn x \map \sgn y

Then: :\operatorname{sgn} \left({x}\right) = \dfrac x {\left\vert{x}\right\vert} = \dfrac {\left\vert{x}\right\vert} x where: :\operatorname{sgn} \left({x}\right) denotes the signum function of x :\left\vert{x}\right\vert denotes the absolute value of x.

Absolute Value Function is Completely Multiplicative: The absolute value function on the real numbers \R is completely multiplicative: :\forall x, y \in \R: \left\vert{x y}\right\vert = \left\vert{x}\right\vert \, \left\vert{y}\right\vert where \left \vert{a}\right \vert denotes the absolute value of a.

Completely Multiplicative Function of Quotient: Let f: \R \to \R be a completely multiplicative function. Then: :\forall x, y \in \R, y \ne 0: f \left({\dfrac x y}\right) = \dfrac {f \left({x}\right)} {f \left({y}\right)} whenever f \left({y}\right) \ne 0.
Signum Function of Reciprocal: Let x \in \R such that x \ne 0. Then: :\map \sgn x = \map \sgn {\dfrac 1 x} where \map \sgn x denotes the signum of x.

Primitive of Reciprocal of a x squared plus b x plus c/a equal to 0: \int \frac {\d x} {a x^2 + b x + c} = \frac 1 b \ln \size {b x + c} + C when a = 0.

Primitive of x over a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {a x^2 + b x + c} = \frac 1 {2 a} \ln \left\vert{a x^2 + b x + c}\right\vert - \frac b {2 a} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {a x^2 + b x + c}
Primitive of Reciprocal of a x squared plus b x plus c/c equal to 0: Let c = 0. Then: : \int \frac {\d x} {a x^2 + b x + c} = \frac 1 b \ln \size {\frac x {a x + b} } + C

Primitive of x squared over a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \frac {x^2 \rd x} {a x^2 + b x + c} = \frac x a - \frac b {2 a^2} \ln \size {a x^2 + b x + c} - \frac {b^2 - 2 a c} {2 a^2} \int \frac {\d x} {a x^2 + b x + c}

Primitive of Power of x over a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \frac {x^m \rd x} {a x^2 + b x + c} = \frac {x^{m - 1} } {\paren {m - 1} a} - \frac b a \int \frac {x^{m - 1} \rd x} {a x^2 + b x + c} - \frac c a \int \frac {x^{m - 2} \rd x} {a x^2 + b x + c}

Primitive of Reciprocal of a x squared plus b x plus c/Negative Discriminant: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Let b^2 - 4 a c < 0. Then: : \int \frac {\d x} {a x^2 + b x + c} = \frac 2 {\sqrt {4 a c - b^2} } \map \arctan {\dfrac {2 a x + b} {\sqrt {4 a c - b^2} } } + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of a x squared plus b x plus c/Positive Discriminant: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Let b^2 - 4 a c > 0. Then: : \int \frac {\d x} {a x^2 + b x + c} = \frac 1 {\sqrt {b^2 - 4 a c} } \ln \size {\dfrac {2 a x + b - \sqrt {b^2 - 4 a c} } {2 a x + b + \sqrt {b^2 - 4 a c} } } + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of a x squared plus b x plus c/Zero Discriminant: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Let b^2 - 4 a c = 0. Then: : \int \frac {\d x} {a x^2 + b x + c} = \frac {-2} {2 a x + b} + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of square of a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x^2 + b x + c}\right)^2} = \frac {2 a x + b} {\left({4 a c - b^2}\right) \left({a x^2 + b x + c}\right)} + \frac {2 a} {4 a c - b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {a x^2 + b x + c}
Completing the Square: Let a, b, c, x be real numbers with a \ne 0. Then: :a x^2 + b x + c = \dfrac {\paren {2 a x + b}^2 + 4 a c - b^2} {4 a} This process is known as completing the square.

Primitive of x over square of a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {\left({a x^2 + b x + c}\right)^2} = \frac {- \left({b x + 2 c}\right)} {\left({4 a c - b^2}\right) \left({a x^2 + b x + c}\right)} - \frac b {4 a c - b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {a x^2 + b x + c}

Primitive of x squared over square of a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \frac {x^2 \ \mathrm d x} {\left({a x^2 + b x + c}\right)^2} = \frac {\left({b^2 - 2 a c}\right) x + b c} {a \left({4 a c - b^2}\right) \left({a x^2 + b x + c}\right)} + \frac {2 c} {4 a c - b^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {a x^2 + b x + c}

Primitive of Reciprocal of x by square of a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {a x^2 + b x + c}^2} = \frac 1 {2 c \paren {a x^2 + b x + c} } - \frac b {2 c} \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a x^2 + b x + c}^2} + \frac 1 c \int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {a x^2 + b x + c} }

Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by square of a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 \paren {a x^2 + b x + c}^2} = \frac {-1} {c x \paren {a x^2 + b x + c} } - \frac {3 a} c \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {a x^2 + b x + c}^2} - \frac {2 b} c \int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {a x^2 + b x + c}^2}
Ring of Sets Closed under Finite Union: Let \mathcal R be a ring of sets. Let A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n \in \mathcal R. Then: : \bigcup_{j \mathop = 1}^n A_j \in \mathcal R

Sigma-Ring contains Limit Superior of Sequence of Sets: Let \mathcal R be a \sigma-ring. Let \left \langle{A_n}\right \rangle_{n \mathop \in \N} \in \mathcal R be a sequence of sets in \mathcal R. Then: : \limsup_{n \to \infty} \ A_n \in \mathcal R
Gamma Function for Non-Negative Integer Argument: The Gamma function satisfies: :\map \Gamma z = \dfrac {\map \Gamma {z + 1} } z for any z which is not a nonpositive integer.

Gamma Function of Positive Half-Integer: {{begin-eqn \Gamma \left({m + \frac 1 2}\right) \frac {\left({2 m}\right)!} {2^{2 m} m!} \sqrt \pi ; r = \frac {1 \times 3 \times 5 \times \cdots \times \left({2 m - 1}\right)} {2^m} \sqrt \pi ; {{end-eqn where: : m + \dfrac 1 2 is a half-integer such that m > 0 : \Gamma denotes the Gamma function.

Gamma Function of Negative Half-Integer: {{begin-eqn \map \Gamma {-m + \frac 1 2} \frac {\paren {-1}^m 2^{2 m} m!} {\paren {2 m}!} \sqrt \pi ; r = \frac {\paren {-1}^m 2^m} {1 \times 3 \times 5 \times \cdots \times \paren {2 m - 1} } \sqrt \pi ; {{end-eqn where: :-m + \dfrac 1 2 is a half-integer such that m > 0 :\Gamma denotes the Gamma function.

Reciprocal times Derivative of Gamma Function: Let \Gamma denote the Gamma function. Then: : \dfrac {\Gamma\,' \left({z}\right)} {\Gamma \left({z}\right)} = -\gamma + \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \left({\frac 1 n - \frac 1 {z + n - 1} }\right) where: : \Gamma\,' \left({z}\right) denotes the derivative of the Gamma function : \gamma denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

Derivative of Gamma Function at 1: Let \Gamma denote the Gamma function. Then: :\map {\Gamma'} 1 = -\gamma where: :\map {\Gamma'} 1 denotes the derivative of the Gamma function evaluated at 1 :\gamma denotes the Euler-Mascheroni constant.

Stirling's Formula for Gamma Function: Let \Gamma denote the Gamma function. Then: :\Gamma \left({x + 1}\right) = \sqrt {2 \pi x} \, x^x e^{-x} \left({1 + \dfrac 1 {12 x} + \dfrac 1 {288 x^2} - \dfrac {139} {51 \, 480 x^3} + \cdots}\right)
Commutativity of Parameters of Beta Function: \map \Beta {x, y} = \map \Beta {y, x}

Beta Function as Integral of Power of t over Power of t plus 1: \map \Beta {x, y} = \int_{\mathop \to 0}^{\mathop \to \infty} \frac {t^{x - 1} } {\paren {1 + t}^{x + y} } \rd t where \Beta denotes the Beta function.

Beta Function as Integral of Power of t by Power of 1 minus t over Power of r plus t: \Beta \left({x, y}\right) := r^y \left({r + 1}\right)^x \int_{\mathop \to 0}^{\mathop \to 1} \frac {t^{x - 1} \left({1 - t}\right)^{y - 1} } {\left({r + t}\right)^{x + y} } \rd t where \Beta denotes the Beta function.

Separation of Variables/General Result: Suppose a first order ordinary differential equation can be expressible in this form: :\map {g_1} x \map {h_1} y + \map {g_2} x \map {h_2} y \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = 0 Then the equation is said to have separable variables, or be separable. Its general solution is found by solving the integration: : \int \frac {\map {g_1} x} {\map {g_2} x} \rd x + \int \frac {\map {h_2} y} {\map {h_1} y} \rd y = C

Sum of Arithmetic-Geometric Sequence: Let \sequence {a_k} be an arithmetic-geometric sequence defined as: :a_k = \paren {a + k d} r^k for k = 0, 1, 2, \ldots, n - 1 Then its closed-form expression is: : \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^{n - 1} \paren {a + k d} r^k = \frac {a \paren {1 - r^n} } {1 - r} + \frac {r d \paren {1 - n r^{n - 1} + \paren {n - 1} r^n} } {\paren {1 - r}^2}

Sum of Infinite Arithmetic-Geometric Sequence: Let \sequence {a_k} be an arithmetic-geometric sequence defined as: :a_k = \paren {a + k d} r^k for n = 0, 1, 2, \ldots Let: :\size r < 1 where \size r denotes the absolute value of r. Then: : \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \paren {a + k d} r^k = \frac a {1 - r} + \frac {r d} {\paren {1 - r}^2}

Reduction Formula for Integral of Power of Cosine: Let n \in \Z_{> 0} be a (strictly) positive integer. Then: : \int \cos^n x \rd x = \dfrac {\cos^{n - 1} x \sin x} n + \dfrac {n - 1} n \int \cos^{n - 2} x \rd x is a reduction formula for \int \cos^n x \rd x.

Primitive of Reciprocal of Root of a x squared plus b x plus c/Negative Discriminant: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Let b^2 - 4 a c < 0. Then: : \int \frac {\d x} {\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } = \frac 1 {\sqrt a} \sinh^{-1} \paren {\dfrac {2 a x + b} {\sqrt {4 a c - b^2} } } + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of Root of a x squared plus b x plus c/Positive Discriminant: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Let b^2 - 4 a c > 0. Then: : \int \frac {\d x} {\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } = \frac 1 {\sqrt a} \map \ln {2 \sqrt a \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} + 2 a x + b} + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of Root of a x squared plus b x plus c/Zero Discriminant: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Let b^2 - 4 a c = 0. Then: : \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } = \frac 1 {\sqrt a} \ln \left\vert{2 a x + b}\right\vert + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of Root of a x squared plus b x plus c/a equal to 0: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } = \frac {2 \sqrt {b x + c} } b + C when a = 0.

Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by Root of a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } = -\frac {\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } {c x} - \frac b {2 c} \int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} }

Primitive of Root of a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} \rd x = \frac {\paren {2 a x + b} \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } {4 a} + \frac {4 a c - b^2} {8 a} \int \frac {\d x} {\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} }

Primitive of x by Root of a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int x \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} \ \mathrm d x = \frac {\left({\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} }\right)^3} {3 a} - \frac {b \left({2 a x + b}\right) \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } {8 a^2} - \frac {b \left({4 a c - b^2}\right)} {16 a^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} }

Primitive of x squared by Root of a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int x^2 \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} \rd x = \frac {6 a x - 5 b} {24 a^2} \paren {\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} }^3 + \frac {5 b^2 - 4 a c} {16 a^2} \int \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} \rd x

Primitive of Root of a x squared plus b x plus c over x: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \frac {\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } x \rd x = \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} + \frac b 2 \int \frac {\d x} {\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } + c \int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} }

Primitive of Root of a x squared plus b x plus c over x squared: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \frac {\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } {x^2} \ \mathrm d x = \frac {-\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } x + a \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } + \frac b 2 \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} }

Primitive of Reciprocal of Cube of Root of a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} }\right)^3} = \frac {2 \left({2 a x + b}\right)} {\left({4 a c - b^2}\right) \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } + C

Primitive of x over Cube of Root of a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {\left({\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} }\right)^3} = \frac {2 \left({b x + 2 c}\right)} {\left({b^2 - 4 a c}\right) \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} }

Primitive of x squared over Cube of Root of a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \frac {x^2 \ \mathrm d x} {\left({\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} }\right)^3} = \frac {\left({2 b^2 - 4 a c}\right) x + 2 b c} {a \left({4 a c - b^2}\right) \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } + \frac 1 a \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} }

Primitive of Reciprocal of x by Cube of Root of a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} }\right)^3} = \frac 1 {c \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } + \frac 1 c \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } - \frac b {2 c} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} }\right)^3}

Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by Cube of Root of a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 \paren {\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} }^3} = -\frac {a x^2 + 2 b x + c} {c^2 x \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} } + \frac {b^2 - 2 a c} {2 c^2} \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {\sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} }^3} - \frac {3 b} {2 c^2} \int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt {a x^2 + b x + c} }

Primitive of Half Integer Power of a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \left({a x^2 + b x + c}\right)^{n + \frac 1 2} \ \mathrm d x = \frac {\left({2 a x + b}\right) \left({a x^2 + b x + c}\right)^{n + \frac 1 2} } {4 a \left({n + 1}\right)} + \frac {\left({2 n + 1}\right) \left({4 a c - b^2}\right)} {8 a \left({n + 1}\right)} \int \left({a x^2 + b x + c}\right)^{n - \frac 1 2} \ \mathrm d x

Primitive of x by Half Integer Power of a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int x \left({a x^2 + b x + c}\right)^{n + \frac 1 2} \ \mathrm d x = \frac {\left({a x^2 + b x + c}\right)^{n + \frac 3 2} } {a \left({2 n + 3}\right)} - \frac b {2 a} \int \left({a x^2 + b x + c}\right)^{n + \frac 1 2} \ \mathrm d x

Primitive of Reciprocal of Half Integer Power of a x squared plus b x plus c: Let a \in \R_{\ne 0}. Then: : \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x^2 + b x + c}\right)^{n + \frac 1 2} } = \frac {2 \left({2 a x + b}\right)} {\left({2 n - 1}\right) \left({4 a c - b^2}\right) \left({a x^2 + b x + c}\right)^{n - \frac 1 2} } + \frac {8 a \left({n - 1}\right)} {\left({2 n - 1}\right) \left({4 a c - b^2}\right)} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({a x^2 + b x + c}\right)^{n - \frac 1 2} }

Primitive of x over x cubed plus a cubed: \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^3 + a^3} = \frac 1 {6 a} \map \ln {\frac {x^2 - a x + a^2} {\paren {x + a}^2} } + \frac 1 {a \sqrt 3} \arctan \frac {2 x - a} {a \sqrt 3}

Primitive of Reciprocal of x cubed plus a cubed: \int \frac {\d x} {x^3 + a^3} = \frac 1 {6 a^2} \ln \size {\frac {\paren {x + a}^2} {x^2 - a x + a^2} } + \frac 1 {a^2 \sqrt 3} \arctan \frac {2 x - a} {a \sqrt 3}
Primitive of x squared over x cubed plus a cubed: \int \frac {x^2 \rd x} {x^3 + a^3} = \frac 1 3 \ln \size {x^3 + a^3} + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of x by x cubed plus a cubed: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)} = \frac 1 {3 a^3} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x^3} {x^3 + a^3} }\right\vert + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by x cubed plus a cubed: \int \frac {\d x} {x^2 \paren {x^3 + a^3} } = \frac {-1} {a^3 x} - \frac 1 {6 a^4} \map \ln {\frac {x^2 - a x + a^2} {\paren {x + a}^2} } - \frac 1 {a^4 \sqrt 3} \arctan \frac {2 x - a} {a \sqrt 3}

Primitive of Reciprocal of x cubed plus a cubed squared: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({x^3 + a^3}\right)^2} = \frac x {3 a^3 \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)} + \frac 1 {9 a^5} \ln \left({\frac {\left({x + a}\right)^2} {x^2 - a x + a^2} }\right) + \frac 2 {3 a^5 \sqrt 3} \arctan \frac {2 x - a} {a \sqrt 3}

Primitive of x over x cubed plus a cubed squared: \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {\left({x^3 + a^3}\right)^2} = \frac {x^2} {3 a^3 \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)} + \frac 1 {18 a^4} \ln \left({\frac {x^2 - a x + a^2} {\left({x + a}\right)^2} }\right) + \frac 1 {3 a^4 \sqrt 3} \arctan \frac {2 x - a} {a \sqrt 3}
Primitive of x squared over x cubed plus a cubed squared: \int \frac {x^2 \ \mathrm d x} {\left({x^3 + a^3}\right)^2} = \frac {-1} {3 \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)} + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of x by x cubed plus a cubed squared: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)^2} = \frac 1 {3 a^3 \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)} + \frac 1 {3 a^6} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x^3} {x^3 + a^3} }\right\vert

Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by x cubed plus a cubed squared: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)^2} = \frac {-1} {a^6 x} - \frac {x^2} {3 a^6 \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)} - \frac 4 {3 a^6} \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {x^3 + a^3}
Primitive of Power of x over x cubed plus a cubed: \int \frac {x^m \rd x} {x^3 + a^3} = \frac {x^{m - 2} } {m - 2} - a^3 \int \frac {x^{m - 3} \rd x} {x^3 + a^3}

Primitive of Reciprocal of x fourth plus a fourth: \int \frac {\d x} {x^4 + a^4} = \frac 1 {4 a^3 \sqrt 2} \map \ln {\frac {x^2 + a x \sqrt 2 + a^2} {x^2 - a x \sqrt 2 + a^2} } - \frac 1 {2 a^3 \sqrt 2} \paren {\map \arctan {1 - \frac {x \sqrt 2} a} - \map \arctan {1 + \frac {x \sqrt 2} a} }
Primitive of x over x fourth plus a fourth: \int \frac {x \rd x} {x^4 + a^4} = \frac 1 {2 a^2} \arctan \frac {x^2} {a^2}

Primitive of x squared over x fourth plus a fourth: \int \frac {x^2 \rd x} {x^4 + a^4} = \frac 1 {4 a \sqrt 2} \map \ln {\frac {x^2 - a x \sqrt 2 + a^2} {x^2 + a x \sqrt 2 + a^2} } - \frac 1 {2 a \sqrt 2} \paren {\map \arctan {1 - \frac {x \sqrt 2} a} - \map \arctan {1 + \frac {x \sqrt 2} a} }
Primitive of x cubed over x fourth plus a fourth: \int \frac {x^3 \ \mathrm d x} {x^4 + a^4} = \frac {\ln \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)} 4
Primitive of Reciprocal of x by x fourth plus a fourth: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)} = \frac 1 {4 a^4} \ln \left({\frac {x^4} {x^4 + a^4} }\right)

Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by x fourth plus a fourth: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)} = \frac {-1} {a^4 x} - \frac {-1} {4 a^5 \sqrt 2} \ln \left({\frac {x^2 - a x \sqrt 2 + a^2} {x^2 + a x \sqrt 2 + a^2} }\right) + \frac 1 {2 a^5 \sqrt 2} \left({\arctan \left({1 - \frac {x \sqrt 2} a}\right) - \arctan \left({1 + \frac {x \sqrt 2} a}\right)}\right)
Primitive of Reciprocal of x cubed by x fourth plus a fourth: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)} = \frac {-1} {2 a^4 x^2} - \frac 1 {2 a^6} \arctan \frac {x^2} {a^2}
Primitive of Reciprocal of x fourth minus a fourth: \int \frac {\d x} {x^4 - a^4} = \frac 1 {4 a^3} \ln \size {\frac {x - a} {x + a} } - \frac 1 {2 a^3} \arctan \frac x a
Primitive of x over x fourth minus a fourth: \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {x^4 - a^4} = \frac 1 {4 a^2} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x^2 - a^2} {x^2 + a^2} }\right\vert + C
Primitive of x squared over x fourth minus a fourth: \int \frac {x^2 \rd x} {x^4 - a^4} = \frac 1 {4 a} \ln \size {\frac {x - a} {x + a} } + \frac 1 {2 a} \arctan \frac x a + C
Primitive of x cubed over x fourth minus a fourth: \int \frac {x^3 \ \mathrm d x} {x^4 - a^4} = \frac {\ln \left\vert{x^4 - a^4}\right\vert} 4 + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of x by x fourth minus a fourth: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)} = \frac 1 {4 a^4} {\ln \left\vert{\frac {x^4 - a^4} {x^4} }\right\vert} + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by x fourth minus a fourth: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)} = \frac 1 {a^4 x} + \frac 1 {4 a^5} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x - a} {x + a} }\right\vert + \frac 1 {2 a^5} \arctan \frac x a + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of x cubed by x fourth minus a fourth: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^3 \left({x^4 - a^4}\right)} = \frac 1 {2 a^4 x^2} + \frac 1 {4 a^6} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x^2 - a^2} {x^2 + a^2} }\right\vert + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of x by Power of x plus Power of a: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x \left({x^n + a^n}\right)} = \frac 1 {n a^n} \ln \left\vert{\frac {x^n} {x^n + a^n} }\right\vert + C
Absolute Value of Even Power: Let x \in \R be a real number. Let n \in \Z be an integer. Then: :\left\vert{x^{2 n} }\right\vert = x^{2 n}
Primitive of Power of x less one over Power of x plus Power of a: \int \frac {x^{n - 1} \ \mathrm d x} {x^n + a^n} = \frac 1 n \ln \left\vert{x^n + a^n}\right\vert + C
Primitive of x cubed over x fourth plus a fourth/Proof 1: \int \frac {x^3 \ \mathrm d x} {x^4 + a^4} = \frac {\ln \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)} 4
Primitive of x cubed over x fourth plus a fourth/Proof 2: \int \frac {x^3 \ \mathrm d x} {x^4 + a^4} = \frac {\ln \left({x^4 + a^4}\right)} 4

Primitive of Reciprocal of Power of x by Power of Power of x plus Power of a: \int \frac {\d x} {x^m \ \left({x^n + a^n}\right)^r} = \frac 1 {a^n} \int \frac {\d x} {x^m \left({x^n + a^n}\right)^{r - 1} } - \frac 1 {a^n} \int \frac {\d x} {x^{m - n} \left({x^n + a^n}\right)^r}

Primitive of Reciprocal of x by Root of Power of x plus Power of a: \int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt {x^n + a^n} } = \frac 1 {n \sqrt {a^n} } \ln \size {\frac {\sqrt {x^n + a^n} - \sqrt {a^n} } {\sqrt {x^n + a^n} + \sqrt {a^n} } } + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of x by Power of x minus Power of a: \int \frac {\d x} {x \paren {x^n - a^n} } = \frac 1 {n a^n} \ln \size {\frac {x^n - a^n} {x^n} } + C
Primitive of Power of x less one over Power of x minus Power of a: \int \frac {x^{n - 1} \rd x} {x^n - a^n} = \frac 1 n \ln \size {x^n - a^n} + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of x by Root of Power of x minus Power of a: \int \frac {\d x} {x \sqrt {x^n - a^n} } = \frac 2 {n \sqrt {a^n} } \arccos \sqrt {\frac {a^n} {x^n} }
Primitive of x by Sine of a x: \int x \sin a x \rd x = \frac {\sin a x} {a^2} - \frac {x \cos a x} a + C
Primitive of x squared by Sine of a x: \int x^2 \sin a x \rd x = \frac {2 x \sin a x} {a^2} + \paren {\frac 2 {a^3} - \frac {x^2} a} \cos a x + C
Primitive of x cubed by Sine of a x: \int x^3 \sin a x \rd x = \paren {\frac {3 x^2} {a^2} - \frac 6 {a^4} } \sin a x + \paren {\frac {6 x} {a^3} - \frac {x^3} a} \cos a x + C

Primitive of Sine of a x over x: {{begin-eqn \int \frac {\sin a x \d x} x \sum_{k \mathop \ge 0} \frac {\paren {-1}^k \paren {a x}^{2 k + 1} } {\paren {2 k + 1} \paren {2 k + 1}!} + C r = a x - \frac {\paren {a x}^3} {3 \times 3!} + \frac {\paren {a x}^5} {5 \times 5!} - \cdots {{end-eqn
Primitive of Sine of a x over x squared: \int \frac {\sin a x \ \mathrm d x} {x^2} = -\frac {\sin a x} x + a \int \frac {\cos a x \ \mathrm d x} x
Primitive of Reciprocal of Sine of a x/Logarithm of Cosecant minus Cotangent Form: \int \frac {\d x} {\sin a x} = \frac 1 a \ln \size {\csc a x - \cot a x} + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of Sine of a x/Logarithm of Tangent Form: \int \frac {\d x} {\sin a x} = \frac 1 a \ln \size {\tan \frac {a x} 2} + C

Primitive of x over Sine of a x: {{begin-eqn \int \frac {x \rd x} {\sin a x} \frac 1 {a^2} \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {\paren {-1}^{n - 1} 2 \paren {2^{2 n - 1} - 1} B_{2 n} \paren {a x}^{2 n + 1} } {\paren {2 n + 1}!} + C ; r = \frac 1 {a^2} \paren {a x + \frac {\paren {a x}^3} {18} + \frac {7 \paren {a x}^5} {1800} \cdots} + C ; {{end-eqn
Primitive of Square of Sine of a x: \int \sin^2 a x \rd x = \frac x 2 - \frac {\sin 2 a x} {4 a} + C
Primitive of x by Square of Sine of a x: \int x \sin^2 a x \rd x = \frac {x^2} 4 - \frac {x \sin 2 a x} {4 a} - \frac {\cos 2 a x} {8 a^2} + C
Primitive of Cube of Sine of a x: \int \sin^3 a x \rd x = -\frac {\cos a x} a + \frac {\cos^3 a x} {3 a} + C
Primitive of Fourth Power of Sine of a x: \int \sin^4 a x \ \mathrm d x = \frac {3 x} 8 - \frac {\sin 2 a x} {4 a} + \frac {\sin 4 a x} {32 a} + C
Primitive of Square of Cosecant of a x: \int \csc^2 a x \ \mathrm d x = -\frac {\cot a x} a + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of Square of Sine of a x: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\sin^2 a x} = \frac {-\cot a x} a + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of Cube of Sine of a x: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\sin^3 a x} = \frac {-\cos a x} {2 a \sin^2 a x} + \frac 1 {2 a} \ln \left\vert{\tan \frac {a x} 2}\right\vert + C
Primitive of Sine of p x by Sine of q x: For p \ne q: : \int \sin p x \sin q x \rd x = \frac {\map \sin {p - q} x} {2 \paren {p - q} } - \frac {\map \sin {p + q} x} {2 \paren {p + q} } + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of 1 minus Sine of a x: \int \frac {\d x} {1 - \sin a x} = \frac 1 a \tan \left({\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2}\right) + C

Primitive of x over 1 minus Sine of a x: \int \frac {x \rd x} {1 - \sin a x} = \frac x a \map \tan {\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2} + \frac 2 {a^2} \ln \size {\map \sin {\frac \pi 4 - \frac {a x} 2} } + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of 1 plus Sine of a x: \int \frac {\d x} {1 + \sin a x} = -\frac 1 a \map \tan {\frac \pi 4 - \frac {a x} 2} + C

Primitive of x over 1 plus Sine of a x: \int \frac {x \rd x} {1 + \sin a x} = -\frac x a \map \tan {\frac \pi 4 - \frac {a x} 2} + \frac 2 {a^2} \ln \size {\map \sin {\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2} } + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of Square of 1 minus Sine of a x: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({1 - \sin a x}\right)^2} = \frac 1 {2 a} \tan \left({\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2}\right) + \frac 1 {6 a} \tan^3 \left({\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2}\right) + C
Reciprocal of One Minus Sine: \dfrac 1 {1 - \sin x} = \dfrac 1 2 \map {\sec^2} {\dfrac \pi 4 + \dfrac x 2}
Reciprocal of One Plus Sine: \dfrac 1 {1 + \sin x} = \dfrac 1 2 \map {\sec^2} {\dfrac \pi 4 - \dfrac x 2}

Power Series Expansion for Cosecant Function: The cosecant function has a Laurent series expansion: {{begin-eqn \csc x \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac {\paren {-1}^{n - 1} 2 \paren {2^{2 n - 1} - 1} B_{2 n} \, x^{2 n - 1} } {\paren {2 n}!} ; r = \frac 1 x + \frac x 6 + \frac {7 x^3} {360} + \frac {31 x^5} {15 \, 120} + \cdots ; {{end-eqn where B_n denotes the Bernoulli numbers. This converges for 0 < \size x < \pi.

Periodic Function plus Constant: Let f: \mathbb F \to \mathbb F be a function, where \mathbb F \in \left\{{\R, \C}\right\}. Let k \in \mathbb F be constant. Then f is periodic with period L {{iff f + k is periodic with period L.
Derivative of Periodic Function: Let f: \R \to \R be a real function. Let f be differentiable on all of \R. Then if f is periodic with period L, then its derivative is also periodic with period L.
Sum of Two Odd Powers/Examples/Sum of Two Cubes: x^3 + y^3 = \paren {x + y} \paren {x^2 - x y + y^2}
Primitive of Periodic Function: Let f: \R \to \R be a real function. Let F be a primitive of f that is bounded on all of \R. Let f be periodic with period L. Then F is also periodic with period L.

Primitive of Reciprocal of x squared by x cubed plus a cubed/Lemma: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {x^2 \left({x^3 + a^3}\right)} = \frac {-1} {a^3 x} - \frac 1 {a^3} \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {\left({x^3 + a^3}\right)}
Sum of Two Fourth Powers: x^4 + y^4 = \paren {x^2 + \sqrt 2 x y + y^2} \paren {x^2 - \sqrt 2 x y + y^2}

Pumping Lemma for Regular Languages: Let \mathcal L_3 be the set of regular languages. {{explain|Is it a set? Does this need to be proved? Intuition would suggest that it would be a class. Then the following holds: \forall L \in \mathcal L_3: \exists n_0 \in \N_0: \forall z \in L: \left|{z}\right| > n_0 \implies \exists u, v, w such that: :z = u \cdot v \cdot w :\left|{v}\right| > 0 :\left|{u v}\right| < n_0 :\forall i \in \N_0: u \cdot v^i \cdot w \in L
One Plus Tangent Half Angle over One Minus Tangent Half Angle: \dfrac {1 + \tan \frac x 2} {1 - \tan \frac x 2} = \sec x + \tan x
Primitive of Power of Cosecant of a x: \int \csc^n a x \ \mathrm d x = \frac{-\csc^{n - 2} a x \cot a x} {a \left({n - 1}\right)} + \frac {n - 2} {n - 1} \int \csc^{n - 2} a x \ \mathrm d x
Primitive of Cosecant of a x/Tangent Form: \int \csc a x \rd x = \frac 1 a \ln \size {\tan \frac {a x} 2} + C where \tan \dfrac {a x} 2 \ne 0.
Primitive of Cosecant of a x/Cosecant minus Cotangent Form: \int \csc a x \rd x = \frac 1 a \ln \size {\csc a x - \cot a x} + C where \csc a x - \cot a x \ne 0.

Primitive of Reciprocal of Square of 1 plus Sine of a x: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({1 + \sin a x}\right)^2} = \frac {-1} {2a} \tan \left({\frac \pi 4 - \frac {a x} 2}\right) - \frac 1 {6 a} \tan^3 \left({\frac \pi 4 - \frac {a x} 2}\right) + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of square of p plus q by Sine of a x: \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {p + q \sin a x}^2} = \frac {q \cos a x} {a \paren {p^2 - q^2} \paren {p + q \sin a x} } + \frac p {p^2 - q^2} \int \frac {\d x} {p + q \sin a x}
Primitive of Reciprocal of p squared plus square of q by Sine of a x: \int \frac {\d x} {p^2 + q^2 \sin^2 a x} = \frac 1 {a p \sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } \arctan \frac {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} \tan a x} p + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of p squared minus square of q by Sine of a x: \int \frac {\d x} {p^2 - q^2 \sin^2 a x} = \begin{cases} \frac 1 {a p \sqrt{p^2 - q^2} } \arctan \frac {\sqrt{p^2 - q^2} \tan a x} p & : p^2 > q^2 \\ \frac 1 {2 a p \sqrt{q^2 - p^2} } \ln \size {\frac {\sqrt {q^2 - p^2} \tan a x + p} {\sqrt {q^2 - p^2} \tan a x - p} } & : p^2 < q^2 \end{cases}
Primitive of Power of x by Sine of a x: \int x^m \sin a x \rd x = \frac {-x^m \cos a x} a + \frac {m x^{m - 1} \sin a x} {a^2} - \frac {m \paren {m - 1} } {a^2} \int x^{m - 2} \sin a x \rd x
Primitive of Sine of a x over Power of x: \int \frac {\sin a x} {x^n} \rd x = \frac {-\sin a x} {\paren {n - 1} x^{n - 1} } + \frac a {n - 1} \int \frac {\cos a x} {x^{n - 1} } \rd x

Primitive of Reciprocal of Power of Sine of a x: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\sin^n a x} = \frac {- \cos a x} {a \left({n - 1}\right) \sin^{n - 1} a x} + \frac {n - 2} {n - 1} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\sin^{n - 2} a x}

Primitive of x over Power of Sine of a x: \int \frac {x \rd x} {\sin^n a x} = \frac {-x \cos a x} {a \paren {n - 1} \sin^{n - 1} a x} - \frac 1 {a^2 \paren {n - 1} \paren {n - 2} \sin^{n - 2} a x} + \frac {n - 2} {n - 1} \int \frac {x \rd x} {\sin^{n - 2} a x}
Primitive of x by Cosine of a x: \int x \cos a x \rd x = \frac {\cos a x} {a^2} + \frac {x \sin a x} a + C
Primitive of x squared by Cosine of a x: \int x^2 \cos a x \rd x = \frac {2 x \cos a x} {a^2} + \paren {\frac {x^2} a - \frac 2 {a^3} } \sin a x + C
Primitive of x cubed by Cosine of a x: \int x^3 \map \cos {a x} \rd x = \paren {\frac {3 x^2} {a^2} - \frac 6 {a^4} } \cos a x + \paren {\frac {x^3} a - \frac {6 x} {a^3} } \sin a x + C

Primitive of Cosine of a x over x: {{begin-eqn \int \frac {\cos a x \rd x} x \ln \size x + \sum_{k \mathop \ge 1} \frac {\paren {-1}^k \paren {a x}^{2 k} } {\paren {2 k} \paren {2 k}!} + C r = \ln \size x - \frac {\paren {a x}^2} {2 \times 2!} + \frac {\paren {a x}^4} {4 \times 4!} - \frac {\paren {a x}^6} {6 \times 6!} - \cdots + C {{end-eqn
Primitive of Cosine of a x over x squared: \int \frac {\cos a x \ \mathrm d x} {x^2} = \frac {-\cos a x} x - a \int \frac {\sin a x \ \mathrm d x} x
Primitive of Reciprocal of Cosine of a x/Logarithm of Secant plus Tangent Form: \int \frac {\d x} {\cos a x} = \frac 1 a \ln \size {\sec a x + \tan a z}
Primitive of Reciprocal of Cosine of a x/Logarithm of Tangent Form: \int \frac {\d x} {\cos a x} = \frac 1 a \ln \size {\map \tan {\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2} } + C

Primitive of x over Cosine of a x: {{begin-eqn \int \frac {x \rd x} {\cos a x} \frac 1 {a^2} \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty \frac {E_n \paren {a x}^{2 n + 2} } {\paren {2 n + 2} \paren {2 n}!} + C ; r = \dfrac 1 {a^2} \paren {\frac {\paren {a x}^2} 2 + \frac {\paren {a x}^4} 8 + \frac {5 \paren {a x}^6} {144} + \cdots} + C ; {{end-eqn
Primitive of Square of Cosine of a x: \int \cos^2 a x \, \mathrm d x = \frac x 2 + \frac {\sin 2 a x} {4 a} + C
Primitive of x by Square of Cosine of a x: \int x \cos^2 a x \ \mathrm d x = \frac {x^2} 4 + \frac {x \sin 2 a x} {4 a} + \frac {\cos 2 a x} {8 a^2} + C
Primitive of Cube of Cosine of a x: \int \cos^3 a x \rd x = \frac {\sin a x} a - \frac {\sin^3 a x} {3 a} + C
Primitive of Fourth Power of Cosine of a x: \int \cos^4 a x \ \mathrm d x = \frac {3 x} 8 + \frac {\sin 2 a x} {4 a} + \frac {\sin 4 a x} {32 a} + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of Square of Cosine of a x: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\cos^2 a x} = \frac {\tan a x} a + C
Primitive of Square of Secant of a x: \int \sec^2 a x \ \mathrm d x = \frac {\tan a x} a + C
Primitive of Secant of a x/Tangent Form: \int \sec a x \rd x = \frac 1 a \ln \size {\map \tan {\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2} } + C where \map \tan {\dfrac \pi 4 + \dfrac {a x} 2} \ne 0.
Primitive of Secant of a x/Secant plus Tangent Form: \int \sec a x \rd x = \frac 1 a \ln \size {\sec a x + \tan a x} + C where \sec a x + \tan a x \ne 0.
Primitive of Power of Secant of a x: \int \sec^n a x \rd x = \frac {\sec^{n - 2} a x \tan a x} {a \paren {n - 1} } + \frac {n - 2} {n - 1} \int \sec^{n - 2} a x \rd x
Primitive of Reciprocal of Cube of Cosine of a x: \int \frac {\d x} {\cos^3 a x} = \frac {\sin a x} {2 a \cos^2 a x} + \frac 1 {2 a} \ln \size {\map \tan {\frac \pi 4 + \frac {a x} 2} } + C
Primitive of Cosine of a x by Cosine of p x: \int \cos a x \cos p x \rd x = \frac {\map \sin {\paren {a - p} x} } {2 \paren {a - p} } + \frac {\map \sin {\paren {a + p} x} } {2 \paren {a + p} } + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of 1 minus Cosine of a x: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {1 - \cos a x} = \frac {-1} a \cot \frac {a x} 2 + C
Primitive of x over 1 minus Cosine of a x: \int \frac {x \rd x} {1 - \cos a x} = \frac {-x} a \cot \frac {a x} 2 + \frac 2 {a^2} \ln \size {\sin \frac {a x} 2} + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of 1 plus Cosine of a x: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {1 + \cos a x} = \frac 1 a \tan \frac {a x} 2 + C
Primitive of x over 1 plus Cosine of a x: \int \frac {x \rd x} {1 + \cos a x} = \frac x a \tan \frac {a x} 2 + \frac 2 {a^2} \ln size {\cos \frac {a x} 2} + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of Square of 1 minus Cosine of a x: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({1 - \cos a x}\right)^2} = \frac {-1} {2a} \cot \frac {a x} 2 - \frac 1 {6 a} \cot^3 \frac {a x} 2 + C
Primitive of Reciprocal of Square of 1 plus Cosine of a x: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\left({1 + \cos a x}\right)^2} = \frac 1 {2a} \tan \frac {a x} 2 + \frac 1 {6 a} \tan^3 \frac {a x} 2 + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of square of p plus q by Cosine of a x: \int \frac {\d x} {\paren {p + q \cos a x}^2} = \frac {q \sin a x} {a \paren {q^2 - p^2} \paren {p + q \cos a x} } - \frac p {q^2 - p^2} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {p + q \cos a x}
Primitive of Reciprocal of p squared plus square of q by Cosine of a x: \int \frac {\d x} {p^2 + q^2 \cos^2 a x} = \frac 1 {a p \sqrt{p^2 + q^2} } \arctan \frac {p \tan a x} {\sqrt {p^2 + q^2} } + C

Primitive of Reciprocal of p squared minus square of q by Cosine of a x: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {p^2 - q^2 \cos^2 a x} = \begin{cases} \frac 1 {a p \sqrt{p^2 - q^2} } \arctan \frac {p \tan a x} {\sqrt{p^2 - q^2} } & : p^2 > q^2 \\ \frac 1 {2 a p \sqrt{q^2 - p^2} } \ln \left\vert{\frac {p \tan a x - \sqrt{q^2 - p^2} } {p \tan a x + \sqrt{q^2 - p^2} } }\right\vert & : p^2 < q^2 \end{cases}
Primitive of Power of x by Cosine of a x: \int x^m \cos a x \rd x = \frac {x^m \sin a x} a + \frac {m x^{m - 1} \cos a x} {a^2} - \frac {m \paren {m - 1} } {a^2} \int x^{m - 2} \cos a x \rd x

Primitive of Reciprocal of Power of Cosine of a x: \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\cos^n a x} = \frac {\sin a x} {a \left({n - 1}\right) \cos^{n - 1} a x} + \frac {n - 2} {n - 1} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\cos^{n - 2} a x}

Primitive of x over Power of Cosine of a x: \int \frac {x \ \mathrm d x} {\cos^n a x} = \frac {x \sin a x} {a \left({n - 1}\right) \cos^{n - 1} a x} - \frac 1 {a^2 \left({n - 1}\right) \left({n - 2}\right) \cos^{n - 2} a x} + \frac {n - 2} {n - 1} \int \frac {\mathrm d x} {\cos^{n - 2} a x} + C
Primitive of Sine of a x by Cosine of a x: \int \sin a x \cos a x \rd x = \frac {\sin^2 a x} {2 a} + C

Primitive of Sine of p x by Cosine of q x: \int \sin p x \cos q x \rd x = \frac {-\cos \left({p - q}\right) x} {2 \left({p - q}\right)} - \frac {\cos \left({p + q}\right) x} {2 \left({p + q}\right)} + C for p, q \in \R: p \ne q
Primitive of Power of Sine of a x by Cosine of a x: \int \sin^n a x \cos a x \rd x = \frac {\sin^{n + 1} a x} {\paren {n + 1} a} + C
Primitive of Power of Cosine of a x by Sine of a x: \int \cos^n a x \sin a x \rd x = \frac {-\cos^{n + 1} a x} {\paren {n + 1} a} + C
